newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: French solo yachtsman says he faced death.
newsitem.headline: French solo yachtsman says he faced death.

text.p: A French round-the-world solo yachtsman whose boat sank in mountainous seas between Australia and Antarctica within an hour of his rescue said after reaching dry land on Wednesday he believed he was going to die.
Raphael Dinelli, 28, scrambled from his sinking yacht into a raft thrown from an Australian rescue plane into frigid seas 1,200 miles southwest Western Australia the day after Christmas.
"One night and one day I stand on my boat and I think ... as the waves crash on me and it is very difficult," Dinelli told reporters after his safe arrival in Hobart early on Wednesday.
"In the night I am thinking if nobody arrives, it is not possible for my boat and me to (survive) and the death is next for me," he said.
Dinelli was picked up after a day in the life raft by Briton Pete Goss, a fellow competitor in the Vendee Globe round-the-world race, who brought the bruised and tired Frenchman to Hobart.
Dinelli was the first of three Vendee competitors to run into difficulties in the stormy seas between Australia and Antarctica.
On Wednesday Frenchman Thierry Dubois, 29, was in a liferaft awaiting pick-up by an Australian navy frigate while a search continued for missing 56-year-old Briton Tony Bullimore.

Their yachts capsized in rough seas on Sunday, about 120 miles south of the area where Dinelli struck trouble, sparking a massive search and rescue effort. Dinelli, who was knee-deep in water when found, said he spent 30 hours in his survival suit awaiting rescue after his craft rolled and lost its mast.
"When the plane put my life raft (in the water), 10 minutes after my boat is sinking," he said. "This is my life. When the plane arrived, the rescue, it is my life."
Dinelli praised the efforts of his British rescuer, and said he would continue to sail.
"I want to, I need to (go) sailing again," he said.
